name: SN Phantom Motorcycle
description: A high-end electric motorcycle with noise-canceling body panels that make it nearly silent at any speed. Originally designed for corporate security pursuit, it found its way onto the civilian market and became the preferred ride of freelancers, couriers, and anyone who needs to move fast without being heard. Sleek, matte-black, and expensive enough that owning one in Tier 1 marks you as either very skilled or very dangerous.
propulsion: Dual electric motor, regenerative braking, noise-canceling shell
cost: Φ8,000 new, Φ3,000-5,000 used, Φ1,500 stolen (no questions)
autonomy: Rider-controlled with stability assist and collision avoidance
armament: None standard. Aftermarket weapon mounts are widely available.
common_usage: Freelancers, corporate security outriders, couriers, anyone who values speed and stealth.
story_hooks: A freelancer's Phantom has a previous owner's biometric lock buried in the firmware — and the previous owner wants it back
Silent motorcycles are being used for coordinated hit-and-run attacks, and every Phantom rider is now a suspect
physical_description: The SN Phantom is a lean, angular frame wrapped in matte-black composite paneling that drinks light rather than reflects it. Its body hums with barely-contained electric potential, reinforced with scuffed carbon-weave fairings and grip-tape footboards worn smooth by heavy use. Rain beads and slides off its noise-dampening surfaces, leaving no trace.
